The peninsula · built, approved and proposed · north up

Detailed World Map

The whole peninsula as one map: the crescent range and its summits, the north valley with its town, lake, river and drive-in, the park as the complete rebuild atlas plans it, the Headland and its harbour, the beach town with its promenade, pier, ferry and skate park, the city on its own second peninsula with its port, the coast highway and its tunnels, the regional rail, and the rocks offshore, the land kept in the bay north-west of the Headland, Beach Road's fork at J1 and South Shore on the coast extension. The entrance plan is drawn in its dashed frame as on its own map, as built under and proposal over. World metres, x east, z south, north up. E is built, A is approved and not yet built, P is proposed. Point at anything on the map, or tap it, to name it.

What the context shows

Along the coast, between the pier and the beach town

  • Tide pools: by the Headland (decided 2 October; bench site to be chosen).
  • Three structures into the sea. The Boardwalk pier at z 6, the lagoon's twin jetties at z 322 to 350, and the beach town's pier at z 440, the built ferry landing kept and shortened (decision 2): the jetties stand 316 m south of the pier and about 80 m north of the beach town's pier.
  • The sunset water stays open. The jetties lie at bearings of 170° to 196° from the pier head and the promenade; the protected sector is 280° to 310°.
  • The approved beach promenade starts inside the channel. The world map runs it from (−103, 330) south; the lagoon's channel spans z 326 to 346 there. It wants to start at the south jetty's root, about z 350, so it walks straight onto the jetty, or to cross the mouth on a footbridge. Your call.
  • The waterfront is inside the beach town. The six buildings it replaces stand within the town's outline (decision 7 on the entrance plan).
  • Yachts go to the Headland. The approved marina is in the Headland's harbour cove, about 600 m north of the lagoon's mouth, which is why the lagoon keeps only the boating centre's small rentals.
  • The rail. The approved regional rail crosses the lagoon on the trestle where the north-east lobe meets the east body, and its park halt reserve stays on land beside the slough.
  • Saddleback behind the bridge. From the south jetty's root, Saddleback (330 m, 1.3 km) stands at bearing 57.5°, directly behind Beach Road's arched bridge and over the bathhouse, about 14.5° up; the bridge's lamps reach about 14°.

How this was drawn

The park is the complete rebuild atlas (park-rebuild-overlay.html), the approved target: its outline, routes A to F, junctions, rides, Kiddieland, attractions, interiors, midway units, service roads, walls, planting bands, Coastal Creek, sightlines and protected anchors, placed in the world by a port of ParkPlan.rebuild_expand_point, the approved expansion's own transform. On the Headland the lighthouse experience, keeper exhibit, aquarium court and harbour come from the section atlas (park-sections.html), which places them on the built Headland; the complete atlas still has the lighthouse experience at (−139.3, −183.1) and its exhibit at (−127.3, −166) in its own coordinates, from before the Headland was built. The section atlas's Boardwalk items (pier, pavilion, fishing retrofit) are already world coordinates and are drawn as they are. The ground is as built. On 30 September a probe of the mounted world cast a ray down every 10 m over the whole peninsula to the first ground (stepping through any building), and the relief, the contours and the coastline are drawn from those heights: metres above the sea, whose surface is y −7.5 in the world, so the plaza stands about 7.5 m up. Point anywhere to read the ground's height. Where the world map and the ground disagree, the ground is what stands: north-west of the Headland the built ground carries a broad lobe of land with its big rounded hill, a round hill at its west tip and rocks offshore, which the world map drew as water until 3 October, when Christina kept them (“we dont want to remove that”, “all of those features are part of the landscape”); both maps now draw them from this probe. The rocks differ: above the water in the game, under it (−11 and −9 m) in the world terrain master. At the beach town's south end Beach Road forks at J1, up round J3's bend and under the highway into the hillside's street down, or down to South Shore (beach town plan pass 16, South Shore plan pass 3); pass 9's climb to the highway is dropped. The south beach front (edit 2 B), the regraded hill (edits 6 and 7), South Shore and the rail on its bench are the world terrain master's and the plans', not the game's, and are drawn over the ground as built. Two peninsulas. On 30 September Christina drew the land on this map: the city stands on a second peninsula of its own, reaching south-west; her line west of the coast highway's southern end, and everything east of it, is the original peninsula; and the spit west of that line, the city's old approach land that the highway's extension crosses to the bridge, can be turned into water. It is drawn hatched as water to come; the ground as built still carries it. East of her line, the inlet between it and the shore as built, about 7 ha, becomes land, so her line is the shore all the way down to the bridge; it is drawn hatched as land to come. Where her line turns east it only rounds out the spur the spit leaves, by about 60 m (about 1.2 ha); the south coast stays as built, and the rest of her line is drawn faint. She chose the same night to lengthen the suspension bridge to land on her shore, about 720 m, and to carry the regional rail on it into the city's terminal, which is raised level with the deck because the deck lands too close to it for the line to come down. The named summits stay where the world map puts them; the built range does not peak there but climbs on eastward, to about 456 m at the map's east edge, and each summit's name gives the ground's height at its point. The towns are as built. Every building and every street in the north town, the beach town and the city is drawn from the same probe, footprint by footprint, in its own colour, and named from the node it was built as. The towns' own maps (Beach Town, North Valley, City Peninsula) are planning diagrams, not to scale, so they are linked above rather than drawn. The town outlines, rail, highway and approved sites are the world map's own data (Coastal Creek is left out: its line there is schematic and at this scale would cross the plaza) (park-world-beyond.html), drawn unchanged; the highway's trough is computed as that map computes it. The pier and its pavilion are ParkPlan's (root x −108, 44 m, at z 6). The clock tower is plaza.tscn's. Inside the dashed frame the as-built base, the planting and every proposal layer are the entrance plan's, pass 18, unchanged. Saddleback's position is the world map's summit at −20° and 1,000 m from the range's centre. The world map draws each ridge spur 950 m out from the range's toe; here a spur stops at the shore, so the headland spur, which would lie wholly over the bay, is left to the built Headland, and the south spur ends at the beach. The ferry starts, in the world map's data, 19 m beyond the public pier's head; it is drawn where the data puts it.
